perfect-competition.def: A market with many buyers and sellers of an identical product, full information about prices and free entry and exit, so each firm is a price taker that cannot change the market price.

long-run-eq.def: In perfect competition, the state in which entry and exit have pushed the price to minimum ATC, so P = MR = MC = minimum ATC and every firm earns zero economic profit.

constant-cost.def: A constant-cost industry is one whose firms' costs do not change as the industry grows or shrinks, so its long-run supply curve is horizontal at minimum ATC. (Increasing- and decreasing-cost industries, whose costs rise or fall with industry size, are an extension.)

allocative-efficiency.def: Producing the quantity at which price equals marginal cost (P = MC), so the value buyers place on the last unit equals the cost of making it and total surplus is as large as it can be.
